World.title: Ford Unveils Two-Story Name Rebuke
World.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Donald Trump's Thursday order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" by unveiling a shoreline billboard Saturday: "Lake Ontario. Now and Always." Wearing a Team Canada soccer jersey, Ford posed near Grimsby. The 24-by-12-foot (7.3-by-3.6 meter) sign sits on 6-foot legs, reaching about 18 feet—roughly two stories. CBS said the blue display also reads in French "Lac Ontario - Aujourd'hui et pour toujours" at Fifty Point Conservation Area. Ford said Trump sought the change because Ontario and Canada were "standing up for ourselves," adding, "Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario." The name comes from the Huron word "oniatarí:io," "lake of shining waters." Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard called the order an attempt to erase Indigenous history. Prime Minister Mark Carney noted the name predates Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence; Trump cannot force Canada to follow. The stunt follows collapsed trade talks and 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods. Trump had branded Ford Prime Minister Carney's "flunky."

USA.title: U.S. Eyes 35% Betancourt Oil Cut
USA.description: The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that the U.S. government plans a 35% passive stake in Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt's North American Blue Energy Partners, citing people involved in the talks, Reuters said. Washington also plans preferential rights to buy 20% of the company's production at cost. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital would structure the investment through penny warrants meant to yield equity without a large cash outlay. The report landed a day after President Donald Trump said the United States had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves through a private-business partnership—about a fifth of the OPEC nation's crude. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell pushed back: "The Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) does not take equity stakes in private companies," saying its role is limited to loans, loan guarantees, or technical assistance. The White House and the company did not immediately comment. A U.S. official told CBS News interim President Delcy Rodriguez granted a private joint venture a 100-year concession on those fields, with Washington controlling 55% via equity and at-cost offtake.

Business.title: Glencore Writes Off Entire Radiant Hit
Business.description: Glencore booked a provision of about $480 million covering its entire net exposure to iron ore trader Radiant World, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Radiant owes Glencore $951 million while Glencore owes Radiant $471 million, the Financial Times reported Saturday citing a Radiant letter; sources confirmed the figures, which include Sapphire Minmetals. Earlier in August Glencore said the exposure was "well below" its $500 million materiality threshold. CEO Gary Nagle told investors the company had halted new business, was exiting remaining contracts, and had taken an unspecified provision. The $480 million charge is about a quarter of average annual EBIT over the past decade from metals and minerals trading, a blow to iron ore marketing head Peter Hill. Late in 2025 Glencore acquired unexercised warrants for a minority Radiant stake. Radiant's letter alleged Glencore reviewed hires, advised fundraising, and suggested trade prices. Glencore called the claims "meritless" and said it "will vigorously contest them." At least five banks have been told some Radiant invoices are not genuine. The U.S. Justice Department and Singapore police are investigating; Radiant has denied wrongdoing.

Technology.title: Socket Sensor Warns Before Tissue Injury
Technology.description: Researchers at Zhejiang University of Technology built a bioinspired sensor layer meant to sit inside a prosthetic socket and flag pressure that can injure residual-limb skin, ScienceAlert reported from a Cyborg and Bionic Systems study. The prototype is not a full limb: it tracks where the socket presses, how hard, and for how long. A haptic pathway reports location and intensity; a pain-inspired pathway sums signals over time using synapse-like transistors that grow more sensitive after an injury-like input. "The device neither feels pain nor creates pain in the user," senior author Huaping Wu told ScienceAlert. "Instead, it reproduces selected information-processing features associated with nociception, including stimulus thresholds, temporal and spatial summation, memory, and sensitization." On a robotic hand, 10 kilopascals for 0.21 seconds was treated as harmless; the same pressure for 0.49 seconds triggered withdrawal, then 0.06 seconds after that event. Fitted at four points in three below-knee sockets, it flagged 86.4% of brief discomfort events and 90.9% of prolonged ones. Wu said a wireless, medical-grade build and larger trials are still required.

Entertainment.title: Dolly’s Wish Mended Cyrus Rift
Entertainment.description: Dolly Parton died Tuesday, August 25, at 80 after a brief battle with cancer, and a National Examiner source on Yahoo says Miley Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus are mourning while pledging to honor her last wishes—including ending the family fighting that had torn them apart. Billy Ray, 65, befriended Parton after 1990s touring and asked her to be godmother when he and then-girlfriend Tish Cyrus expected Miley; Parton told Howard Stern in 2023 she was “honored” and stayed “very, very close.” The source says Dolly was “a guiding light,” pushed Miley’s sobriety, and gave Billy Ray tough love with understanding. Examiner reports she “played a big part in helping” Billy Ray and Miley, 33, “patch things up” when their relationship hit “rock bottom,” while loving siblings Brandi, Trace, Christopher, Braison, and Noah. Both have promised to live in ways that would make her proud after the “Jolene” singer’s death.

Sports.title: Messi’s Poker Ends Miami Drought
Sports.description: Lionel Messi scored four goals as Inter Miami thrashed CF Montréal 7-1 on Saturday, Yahoo Sports reports, lifting him to 17 goals and the MLS Golden Boot lead ahead of FC Dallas’ Petar Musa. Two strikes were free kicks: a 40th-minute curler mishandled by Montréal’s defense restored the lead, and a stoppage-time free kick cleared the wall into the right side of the net. Early in the second half he powered through traffic; in the 83rd he chipped goalkeeper Thomas Gillier. It was Messi’s first four-goal MLS haul after hat tricks versus New England (2024) and Nashville (2025). Miami’s seven goals set a franchise single-game record and snapped a winless MLS run since July 25. The Herons have 56 regular-season goals but trail Eastern Conference leaders Nashville by 10 points. MARCA notes Casemiro’s first club goal, Messi’s assist to Luis Suárez, and teen Alexander Shaw’s late long-range strike in the rout.

Science.title: Cancer CAR-T Puts Arthritis In Remission
Science.description: Charité researchers in Berlin tested CD19 CAR T-cell therapy in six people with severe, treatment-refractory rheumatoid arthritis, the world's first such trial, ScienceDaily reported from a Nature Medicine paper dated Aug. 29. Three women and three men, ages 31 to 69, had failed as many as eight targeted or biologic therapies over a decade. Doctors collected each patient's T cells, engineered them to hunt the CD19 marker on disease-driving B cells, gave brief preparatory chemotherapy, then a single infusion. Disease activity fell in all six. Over follow-up of up to one year, three stayed in medication-free remission. The modified cells reached B cells in bone marrow, lymph nodes, and joint tissue. Autoantibodies dropped; vaccine antibodies to chickenpox and tetanus remained. One patient's disease returned after an initial medication-free stretch. Safety: only temporary mild-to-moderate cytokine release syndrome, no severe neurological events. Phase two will add ten patients and compare CAR T with an approved B-cell drug. Kyverna supported the study but did not design or analyze it.

Crypto.title: Spot Cash, Not Leverage, Fuels BTC
Crypto.description: Blockonomi cites QCP Capital arguing Bitcoin’s climb from about $63,500 toward $80,000—briefly above $81,000—rested on spot support, not crowded leverage. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw roughly $2.8 billion in net inflows over eight straight sessions, while BTC-denominated futures open interest fell from about 646,000 BTC in mid-August to around 588,000 BTC and funding stayed subdued, pointing to short covering and cash buying. Options call skew strengthened with put-call below one, yet QCP says positioning was not blow-off leveraged. Macro risk rose after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech; July headline PCE was 3.7% and core 3.3%, and September hike odds jumped to about 56%–60% from roughly 35%, with BTC slipping below $78,000. Treasury plans to lift long-end liquidity buybacks to at least $4 billion from Sept. 9. Against that backdrop, QCP flags $81,000–$86,000 as the next key zone traders should watch.

AI.title: Musk Says Grid Gear Strands GPUs
AI.description: Elon Musk posted on X on August 29, 2026 that roughly 15 gigawatts of AI computing capacity due online in 2027 will likely sit dark because power infrastructure will not be ready. Crypto Briefing reports he blamed transformers, wiring, liquid-cooling loops, and high-capacity networking—not chips. High-voltage transformers now carry 48-to-60-month lead times; North American grid interconnection queues and permitting add further delay. Analysts estimate U.S. data center power demand could reach 66 GW by 2027; leaving 15 GW unpowered would slow industry deployment. SpaceX, public earlier in 2026, closed Q2 with 1.4 GW of compute—up from 1 GW in Q1 and 400 MW a year earlier—aims to exceed 2 GW by year-end 2026, and targets 20 GW of power-and-cooling by end-2027, with Musk calling about 15 GW more realistic. Memphis Colossus under xAI is central; Nvidia Vera Rubin chips and possible Microsoft offtake are flagged. Idle clusters burn fast depreciation on expensive GPUs.

Cosmos/Astronomy.title: Dragon Oxidizer Leak Delays Crew-13
Cosmos/Astronomy.description: NASA and SpaceX are adjusting the Crew-13 launch to the International Space Station after an oxidizer leak on Dragon’s propulsion system was found during standard prelaunch processing, NASA said August 29, 2026. Joint NASA and SpaceX teams are running additional tests and data review and will complete any necessary rework before flight; a new target date will be announced once available. NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will serve as commander and pilot, joined by CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov as mission specialists. After docking, Crew-13 joins Expedition 75. The crew enters quarantine about two weeks before flight from Johnson Space Center in Houston. Liftoff is planned aboard SpaceX’s Dragon on a Falcon 9 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. An August 5 training photo shows the four with their mission plaque inside a station-module mockup.

Health.title: Statins Cut Over-70 Heart Risk 30%
Health.description: A world-first Australian-led trial finds daily cholesterol-lowering statins can cut heart attack or stroke risk in otherwise healthy people over 70, with low serious side-effect risk, The Guardian reports. Statins are already common under 75 for diabetes or high cholesterol and after major heart events at any age; benefit for healthy over-70s without prior events was unclear. Monash researchers randomized nearly 10,000 adults over 70—enrolled via almost 3,400 Australian GPs—to daily statin or placebo. Over nearly six years, first major cardiovascular events fell 30%, or one event prevented per 37 older adults treated. Findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at the European Society of Cardiology Congress in Germany. Co-author Adjunct Prof Mark Nelson stressed age as the biggest risk driver; lead Adjunct Prof Sophia Zoungas hopes guidelines update. Cardiologist Prof Tom Marwick said dementia rates did not differ—countering misinformation—but disability-free survival was unchanged and over 15% discontinued therapy.
